fixes.explanation: Nice thought, baker, but David never asks for that here. He prays, "Save me, O God, by Your name, and vindicate me by Your might!" He wants to be saved and vindicated, and Saul's forgiveness never comes up in this song. Sometimes I add extra chips to a recipe that never asked for them, so I get the urge.
David doesn't mention being sick anywhere in this song. He says, "For strangers rise up against me, and ruthless men seek my life…" His trouble is men who seek his life, not an illness.

That's a good-sounding answer, but it's not in this song. David's promise here is, "Freely I will sacrifice to You…" He never mentions building a house of cedar in this psalm. Here it's just a free sacrifice.
